summary.text: Saritha Komatireddy is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for Attorney General, running a law-and-order campaign against incumbent Letitia James. A Brooklyn-born lawyer and Harvard Law School graduate, she was an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Eastern District of New York for more than a decade, served as chief of staff of the Drug Enforcement Administration, and is a partner at the law firm Holtzman Vogel. She has not previously run for elected office.

paragraphs.text: Born in Brooklyn (Coney Island) to parents who emigrated from India in the 1980s; lives on the Upper East Side and is the mother of four.
Graduated cum laude from Harvard University and magna cum laude from Harvard Law School, where she served on the Harvard Law Review.

Clerked for then-Judge Brett Kavanaugh on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit, 2009–2010; then served as counsel to the National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling (2010–2011) and as an associate at a Washington, D.C. litigation firm, Kellogg, Hansen, Todd, Figel & Frederick (2011–2013).

Served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Eastern District of New York for more than a decade, until late 2025, where her leadership roles included Chief of International Narcotics and Money Laundering, Deputy Chief of Appeals and Deputy Chief of General Crimes; her firm biography says she led cases involving terrorism, cybercrime, money laundering, foreign public corruption, violent gangs and narcotics.

According to her firm biography, she received awards including Attorney General's Distinguished Service Awards (2022, 2023) and the Federal Law Enforcement Foundation Prosecutor of the Year Award (2023, 2024).
Has taught as a Lecturer in Law at Columbia Law School and, previously, as an adjunct professor at George Washington University Law School.

Nominated by President Trump in 2020 to a judgeship on the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York; the nomination was returned to the president, unconfirmed, at the Senate's adjournment on January 3, 2021.
Served as Chief of Staff of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration during the Biden administration.
Became a partner at Holtzman Vogel and received the Republican nomination for Attorney General in February 2026; this is her first run for elected office.
